_comment: Work Lamar puts your way. Edited here, reloaded on script start.
ORDER MATTERS. He works down this list in the order it is written and offers you the
first one you have not finished. Only once every job here is behind you does he stop
deciding and let you pick. Finished jobs are remembered by id in the save, so adding a
job or moving one does not re-lock work you have already done.
id          stable key; never change it once a save references it
kind        BikeRide | RideOut | Hit | DriveBy
BikeRide  the scripted push-bike job -- fixed route, no guns on either side
RideOut   ride out, hands only, both sides
Hit       same trip, everybody armed, the corner shoots back
DriveBy   take a car past and shoot it up without stopping
name        the choice he offers you, in his words
brief       what he says when he explains it
done        what he says when you come back paid
targetGang  whose people you are going after -- their models and colours are used
zone        GET_NAME_OF_ZONE code the job happens in, used for the objective wording
x, y, z     the exact corner they stand on. Leave all three at 0 and the job falls back
to the middle of the zone, which for a big zone can be a block away from the
place you actually meant. BikeRide ignores these -- its route is fixed.
targets     how many of them are waiting
homies      how many of yours ride out with you
escapeHeat  true if the law turns up once the work is done. Lamar will not take it off
you until the stars are gone, so the trip home is part of the job.
heatStars   how many stars escapeHeat applies. Ignored when escapeHeat is false.
payMin/payMax  cash, rolled between the two
rep         standing with your own gang for finishing it
minRank     rank before he will offer it at all

missions.name: Come take a ride with me.
missions.brief: Them Ballas been up on the Chamberlain courts all week actin' like they got a lease on it. Ain't a soul been able to hoop down there since Tuesday.
missions.done: HA! Look at you! That's how we used to do it, boy. My hand still hurt.
briefMore: And we ain't shootin' nobody over no basketball court. You put somethin' out there and the law's on this whole block by dinner, over a COURT. That's how people lose everything on account of nothing.
So get a bike, roll out with the homies, and we handle it like we was fifteen. Hands. That's it. You pull somethin' out there and I ain't never met you.

missions.name: Ride through Rancho and lose the car.
missions.brief: Rancho's full of yellow and they ain't just standin' out there -- they sellin'. In Chamberlain. On Davis. Corners we been on since 'fore you could drive, and I can't touch they price 'cause they gettin' it straight off Madrazo's people.
missions.done: Seen the smoke from the freeway, homie. And ain't nobody got a plate to run, ain't nobody got a body to catch. Vagos gon' sit on they hands and wonder. That's exactly what I wanted.
briefMore: I asked Stretch about it. Man looked me in my face and said leave it alone. So this ain't through him, it's me and you -- and we ain't droppin' nobody neither. Set's in pieces since Grove went purple, we can't win no war. It's a message.

Take the beater out front, roll through Jamestown, and soon as one of 'em looks up you gone. Then the car goes -- out to that lot by the water in La Puerta, gas over it, put a round in it. Law looks for a plate, homie, not a face. Then walk back.

missions.name: Go put our set up.
missions.brief: You seen this fool UNIT? Big red letters, Forum all the way down to the wash. He from Ballas way and he treat this whole side like it's his sketchpad.
missions.done: Drove past the one by the wash this mornin'. Straight over the top of him. He gon' see that and he gon' feel somethin', trust me.
briefMore: Meanwhile our set ain't nowhere. That's how a block stops bein' yours, homie -- not a shootin', just a kid growin' up here who never once seen our name on a wall.
So get a bike, get a can, go over the top of him. Four walls, all local. And go by yourself -- two dudes on bikes with cans is a whole story, one dude is a kid.

missions.name: Rancho. Vagos.
missions.brief: Vagos got a lil spot out Rancho where they break the weight down before it comes our way. Five of 'em out there postin' up like it's a barbecue.
missions.done: I heard about that before you even got back. Whole block heard. Take that.
briefMore: Take that off 'em and they price goes up, and soon as they price goes up ours starts makin' sense again. That's the whole thing. That's the only thing.
Three homies, everybody with a machine pistol -- don't be takin' no shotgun, this ain't huntin'. Somebody always calls the law, so lose 'em before you come back.

missions.name: Ballas on Grove.
missions.brief: Ballas standin' on Grove. On GROVE. My granddaddy's street, homie.
missions.done: THAT'S what I'm talkin' about! Word travels, homie. Word travels.
briefMore: And I know it's theirs on paper, everybody know that. But there's a difference between it bein' theirs and them STANDIN' on it -- let 'em post up and the old heads stop callin' it ours at all. Then it really is gone.
It's two of 'em. Take three homies and everybody carry. You gon' pick up the law on the way out, so don't you bring it back round here.

missions.name: The Vagos need reminding.
missions.brief: La Mesa. Vagos been runnin' packs through there all month -- same weight, half the price, and every dollar of it comin' off our corners.
missions.done: That'll hold 'em a minute. They gon' be lookin' over they shoulder all week.
briefMore: We took the Rancho spot and they just moved it. Can't keep takin' spots off people who got more spots than us, so we make the ROUTE cost 'em instead.
Drive through, make some noise, be gone 'fore the law finish they donut. You ain't gotta be out there all day. It's a message, not a visit.
